# Google Ads Audit Checklist
URL: https://advmarketing.biz/google-ads-audit-malaysia
==============================================================================

Google Ads Audit Checklist for Malaysia (2026) | ADV

← All guides & resources

Google Ads Audit · 2026 Checklist

## The Google Ads Audit Checklist We Use

Eleven checks, in the order we run them on every account that comes to us for a free audit. Do it yourself in an afternoon, or send us view-only access to Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager and Search Console and we will run it for you.

Get a Free Account Audit
Start the Checklist

"If the conversions aren't real, every other number in the account is fiction."

The short answer

A Google Ads audit checks, in order, whether the account counts real leads or sales, whether its money reaches the right searches, and whether its settings let automated bidding learn. Start with conversion tracking, because every other number depends on it, then work through search terms, match types, bidding, budget, ads, landing pages, location settings, Performance Max and account access.

Time needed: about three to four hours for a typical small to mid-size Malaysian account, using the 11 checks below.

How to use this checklist

### How do you audit a Google Ads account?

Work through the checks in order. Each one says what to look at, where it sits in Google Ads, what bad looks like, and how long it takes. Order matters: if check 1 fails, the numbers in checks 2 to 11 are not telling you the truth.

The audit, ticked in sequence

It is the pre-takeover audit from our guide to fixing Google Ads accounts , laid out so you can run it yourself. Or hand it to our Google Ads management team and we run it free.

Part 1 · The data

### What should you check first in a Google Ads audit?

The data. Smart bidding chases whatever the account calls a conversion, so a broken definition spoils every later finding.

01

#### Conversion tracking: is what is counted real?

About 30 to 45 min

Look at Every conversion action, whether it is Primary or Secondary, and what it fires on. Primary actions fill the Conversions column and drive bidding. Secondary actions are observation only (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Goals menu, then Conversions, then Summary.
Bad looks like Page views or WhatsApp icon clicks counted as primary conversions next to real leads. Two tags firing for one lead. More conversions than the enquiries your team actually received.

If this fails, fix it before anything else. Our Google Ads conversion tracking guide covers the setup.

02

#### Account structure and campaign types

About 15 min

Look at Which campaign types are running, how budget splits between them, and whether brand searches sit apart from generic ones.
Where The Campaigns table, last 90 days.
Bad looks like Many small campaigns, each too thin to learn. Brand and generic keywords mixed together, so cheap brand clicks hide an expensive generic campaign.

Part 2 · The waste

### How do you find wasted spend in a Google Ads account?

Read what people really searched, then check that keywords and ads are tight enough to earn good Quality Scores.

03

#### Search terms and negative keywords

About 30 to 60 min

Look at What people actually typed before clicking, over 90 days, sorted by cost. A keyword is what you bid on. A search term is what they searched (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Campaigns, then Insights and reports, then Search terms.
Bad looks like Spend on job seekers ("jawatan kosong"), freebie hunters, DIY searches or places you do not serve, in English and in Malay. A negative keyword list nobody has touched for months.

04

#### Match types, ad relevance and Quality Score

About 20 min

Look at The mix of broad, phrase and exact match, and Quality Score. Its three components are expected clickthrough rate, ad relevance and landing page experience, each rated Above average, Average or Below average (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Keywords, then the columns icon, then the Quality score section.
Bad looks like Broad match on manual bidding, when Google says it is critical to use Smart Bidding with broad match. Top spending keywords rated Below average on the same component, which shows you what to fix.

Part 3 · The engine

### Are bidding and budget set up so the account can learn?

Automated bidding needs conversions to work with. Budget only helps if you are losing impressions to budget.

05

#### Bidding strategy versus conversion volume

About 10 min

Look at Each campaign's bid strategy, set against the conversions it actually records each month.
Where Each campaign's settings, under Bidding.
Bad looks like A Target CPA campaign with a handful of conversions a month, or targets edited every few days. Google recommends judging Target CPA over the last 30 days with at least 30 conversions (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).

06

#### Budget and impression share

About 10 min

Look at Why your ads did not show. Search lost IS (budget) and Search lost IS (rank) split the reason, and both are campaign level columns (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Add both as columns in the Campaigns table.
Bad looks like Your best campaign losing impressions to budget while a weak one has money to spare. Heavy loss to rank, which means Quality Score or bids, so a bigger budget will not fix it.

For realistic RM budgets, see our Google Ads pricing guide and what ads cost in Malaysia .

Part 4 · The offer

### Do the ads and landing pages earn the click?

Both feed Quality Score, so both affect what you pay per click.

07

#### Ads and assets

About 20 min

Look at Your responsive search ads and the assets around them. Each ad takes up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions, and Ad strength is rated from Poor to Excellent (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where The Ads view and the Assets view.
Bad looks like One ad per ad group with three headlines. Promotions that ended months ago. An old number in a call asset. No mention of WhatsApp, when that is how most Malaysian customers want to reach you.

08

#### Landing page and speed

About 15 min

Look at Where each ad sends people, whether the page answers the search, and how it loads on a phone.
Where Campaigns, then Insights and reports, then Landing pages. Check the Mobile-friendly click rate column.
Bad looks like Every ad pointing at the homepage. Slow loading on mobile data. Eight-field forms. Google calls landing page speed one of the easiest ways to improve mobile ad results (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).

Part 5 · The settings

### Which settings quietly leak budget in Malaysia?

Three quick checks that most accounts we review have skipped.

09

#### Location targeting: Presence or Presence or interest

About 5 min

Look at "Presence or interest" is the default and reaches people in, regularly in, or who have shown interest in your targeted locations. "Presence" reaches people in or regularly in them (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Where Each campaign's settings, under Locations.
Bad looks like A Petaling Jaya clinic left on the default, reaching people outside its area who only searched about it. With Singapore next door and many Malaysians searching from abroad, that traffic is real. Local service businesses usually want Presence. Travel, property and education businesses selling overseas may want the default.

10

#### Performance Max checks

About 20 to 30 min

Look at Which searches Performance Max is matching, and whether it is taking your own brand searches.
Where Campaigns, then Search terms, then "Search terms and landing pages for Performance Max". Negative keywords in Performance Max only apply to Search and Shopping inventory (Source: Google Ads Help, 2026).
Bad looks like Most conversions coming from your own brand name, with no brand exclusions set. Asset groups with one image and generic text. Nobody checking overlap with Search.

More in our Performance Max guide .

11

#### Change history, access and ownership

About 10 to 15 min

Look at What changed recently, who can get into the account, and whose account it really is.
Where Campaigns menu, then Change history, which covers the past 2 years. Admin menu, then Access and security.
Bad looks like Performance swings after changes or auto-applied recommendations nobody approved. A former agency or staff member still holding Admin. Only one admin, which Google itself flags as a risk. An account under someone else's login.

After the audit

### What does a cleaned-up account look like?

An audit is a list of problems. Results come from fixing them and managing the account every week. One example of where sustained cleanup can lead is an insurance and fintech platform we manage.

Over 12 months, cost per lead fell 45% from RM4.40 to RM2.41, while leads grew from 1,336 a month to 6,586 in the peak month and spend scaled from RM5,000 to RM20,000 a month. That was a year of tracking fixes, search term work and weekly optimisation. The audit was the starting point, not the cause.

Current numbers are on our Live Results Board , updated weekly.

- A short summary of the issues costing you the most.

Common questions

### Google Ads audit questions, answered.

Straight answers on time, order, location settings and what an audit can and cannot do.

How long does a Google Ads audit take?
+

About three to four hours for a typical small to mid-size Malaysian account. The search terms review takes the longest. Accounts with many campaigns take longer.

What should I check first in a Google Ads audit?
+

Conversion tracking. Smart bidding optimises toward whatever the account counts as a conversion, so if page views or button clicks count as leads, every other number is misleading. Fix the data before touching bids, budgets or keywords.

Should I use Presence or Presence or interest in Malaysia?
+

If you only serve customers physically in your area, Presence is usually safer. The default, Presence or interest, also reaches people elsewhere who have shown interest in your location, which can suit travel, property and education businesses selling overseas.

Is the ADV Google Ads audit really free?
+

Yes. Send us view-only access to Google Ads, Google Analytics 4, Google Tag Manager and Search Console. View-only means we can see campaigns, tags and reports without changing anything. You keep the findings whether or not you hire us. No obligation and no pitch deck.

Can an audit alone lower my cost per lead?
+

No. An audit tells you what to fix and in what order. Savings come from making the fixes and managing the account every week. Our insurance and fintech account took 12 months of sustained work to bring cost per lead from RM4.40 to RM2.41.

# SEO vs AEO vs GEO in Malaysia — Guide
URL: https://advmarketing.biz/seo-aeo-geo-malaysia
==============================================================================

SEO vs AEO vs GEO Malaysia — Get Found & Cited by AI | ADV

← All guides & resources

SEO · AEO · GEO · 2026 Guide

## Found on Google. Cited by AI.

Your customers now ask ChatGPT and Google's AI Overviews before they ever see a list of links. This is how SEO, AEO and GEO fit together, why AI skips most Malaysian websites, and the four layers we build so a business gets ranked and named — with the numbers from doing it.

Get a Free AI Visibility Check
Read the Guide

"Ranking gets you listed. Being cited gets you chosen."

The short answer

SEO gets your page ranked in Google's links. AEO gets your answer lifted into the reply — featured snippets and AI Overviews. GEO gets your brand named inside ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. They are layers of one job, not three separate services.

AI engines retrieve from search indexes — Google's, and largely Bing's for ChatGPT search — so a page that cannot rank is rarely cited. What decides who gets picked is whether the content is crawlable, answers the question directly, comes from a business the engine can recognise, and contains something specific enough to cite.

Realistic timeline: technical fixes in days, Google positions over 4–8 weeks, AI citations measured monthly against a fixed question set.

Why AI skips most sites

### Ranking is not the same as being named.

The same business, the same 20 questions a buyer would ask — and a different answer from every engine. Four gaps explain most of the difference.

#### 1. AI crawlers are blocked

Often by accident — an old robots.txt rule, or a hosting default. Cloudflare offers an AI-crawler block during setup; we found it switched on while moving our own site in September 2026.

#### 2. The answer is buried

Answer engines lift a paragraph, not a page. If the direct answer sits under three paragraphs of brand story, a competitor's clearer sentence gets used instead.

#### 3. The business isn't an entity

No Organization schema, a different name on Google Business Profile, directories and socials. If an AI can't be sure who you are, it names someone it is sure about.

#### 4. Nothing worth citing

"Award-winning, results-driven" gives an AI nothing to quote. Specific, dated, sourced numbers do — it's why our statistics page reached page 1 before any of our service pages.

What we build

### Four layers. Crawlable first.

The four layers, in order

Layer 1 — Crawlable. Allow search and AI crawlers in robots.txt, publish an llms.txt file, make sure pages render without JavaScript, and submit the sitemap to both Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools. ChatGPT search leans heavily on Bing's index, so Bing is not optional.

Layer 2 — Answerable. Put a direct two-to-three-sentence answer at the top of every page, use question-shaped headings, and add FAQ and HowTo schema that matches the visible text word for word. Every guide on this site opens with a "short answer" box for exactly this reason.

Layer 3 — Recognisable. Build one entity graph — Organization and Person schema linked with sameAs to LinkedIn, Google Business Profile and directories — and keep the business name, address and phone identical everywhere.

Layer 4 — Citable. Publish original, dated, sourced data — statistics pages, published results, expert quotes in the press — then measure a fixed question set every month. Our Malaysia statistics page and Live Results Board are both built to be quoted.

What this has produced

5 weeks

To move our own site from an average Google position of ~60 to ~12, Aug → Sep 2026

Page 1

For our statistics research page — 154 impressions in one week at position 6

13 / 20

Buying-intent questions where Perplexity names our healthcare client

20 / 20

Of those questions now show a Google AI Overview above the links

Common questions

### What Malaysian businesses ask about AI search.

The questions we hear most from owners who've noticed customers asking ChatGPT instead of Google.

What is the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?
+

SEO gets your page ranked in Google's list of links. AEO (answer engine optimisation) gets your answer lifted straight into the reply — featured snippets, Google AI Overviews and voice answers. GEO (generative engine optimisation) gets your brand named and cited inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google's AI Mode. They are layers of the same job, not alternatives.

Do I still need SEO if customers ask ChatGPT instead of Google?
+

Yes. AI answer engines retrieve from search indexes — Google's for AI Overviews, and largely Bing's for ChatGPT search — so a page that cannot rank is rarely cited. SEO is the entry ticket; AEO and GEO decide whether you are the source that gets picked.

Should I block AI crawlers from my website?
+

Not if you want to be recommended. Blocking GPTBot, ClaudeBot or PerplexityBot removes you from the answers those tools give. Check your robots.txt and your hosting or CDN settings — Cloudflare offers an AI-crawler block toggle during setup that is easy to leave on by accident.

How long does AEO and GEO take in Malaysia?
+

Technical fixes — crawler access, llms.txt, schema, answer blocks — take days. Google positions typically move over 4 to 8 weeks; our own site went from an average position of about 60 to about 12 in five weeks. AI citations shift more unevenly, which is why we re-test a fixed question set every month.

How do you measure AI visibility?
+

A fixed set of 20 buying-intent questions is run through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google every month, recording whether the brand is named and in what position. Alongside that, AI referral traffic (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai) is tracked as its own channel in Google Analytics.

Can I do AEO and GEO myself?
+

The first two layers, yes: open your site to crawlers, and put a clear two-to-three-sentence answer at the top of every important page. Building a recognisable entity and earning citations from original data and press takes longer and benefits from someone doing it every week.

Get started

### Does AI recommend you, or a competitor?

Send us your website and five questions your customers ask. We'll run them through ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google and show you who gets named — you or someone else. Free, and the findings are yours either way.

SEO Agency Kuala Lumpur — SEO, AEO & GEO Malaysia | ADV

SEO · AEO · GEO

## SEO Agency Kuala Lumpur

We don't just rank your website on Google — we make your brand the answer AI tools cite when your customers ask the questions that matter.

Get a Free SEO Audit
See Our Services

"Ranking on Google was the game. Being cited by AI is the new game. We play both."

What We Deliver

### Six disciplines. One cohesive system.

Most SEO agencies pick one lane. We run technical SEO, content, links, local, and the two new disciplines — AEO and GEO — as a single, coordinated strategy.

#### Technical SEO

Site speed, Core Web Vitals, crawlability, schema markup, XML sitemaps, canonical tags. We fix the foundation so every other piece of SEO work compounds on solid ground.

#### On-Page SEO

Keyword mapping, title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure, content optimisation. Every page built to match search intent — not just keyword density.

#### Link Building

High-DR backlinks through PR placements, industry citations, and content-led outreach. No link farms, no PBNs — only links that build real authority.

#### Answer Engine Optimisation (AEO)

Structured FAQ content, entity definition pages, and JSON-LD schema so ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini cite your brand when users ask the questions you need to own.

#### Generative Engine Optimisation (GEO)

AI Overview inclusion strategies, E-E-A-T signals, and brand entity building for Google's generative search results. We optimise for the summaries that now appear above organic rankings.

#### Local SEO

Google Business Profile optimisation, local citations, and Malaysia-specific keyword targeting for Kuala Lumpur and beyond. Built for businesses that need to be found in a specific place.

The shift

### Most SEO agencies are still optimising for 2019.

Traditional SEO — ranking in Google's blue links for clicks — is still important. We do it well. But the way buyers discover answers is changing faster than most agencies are prepared to admit.

ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews are now first touchpoints for millions of searches. When someone asks "who is the best digital marketing agency in KL?" they're increasingly asking an AI — not typing into a search bar.

AEO and GEO are the layers ADV adds on top of standard SEO: content structured so AI tools can extract it, a brand that reads as a recognised entity, and inclusion in generative summaries — not just a ranking.

We run the same schema, entity, and structured-content work on our own site that we build for clients — we don't recommend what we don't do ourselves.

The Three Layers

### How modern search visibility is built.

ADV doesn't treat SEO, AEO, and GEO as separate services. They are three compounding layers of the same visibility strategy — each one amplifying the others. Read the full guide: SEO vs AEO vs GEO in Malaysia →

Common questions

### SEO questions, answered honestly.

If your question isn't covered here, message us on WhatsApp — we reply fast and we'll give you a straight answer.

How long does SEO take to show results in Malaysia?
+

Technical SEO fixes typically take 2–4 weeks to be indexed and reflect improvements. For rankings, expect 3–6 months for competitive terms in Malaysia — faster for long-tail keywords and local queries. Local SEO for Kuala Lumpur-based terms can show movement within 4–8 weeks when Google Business Profile and citation signals are properly set up.

What's AEO and why does it matter now?
+

AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation) structures your content so AI tools like ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google Gemini can extract and cite your brand as the answer to relevant questions. As more searches now begin inside AI tools rather than traditional search, being cited there is becoming as important as ranking on Google. ADV implements AEO through structured FAQ content, entity definition pages, and JSON-LD schema markup. The SEO vs AEO vs GEO guide walks through how it works.

What's GEO?
+

GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation) focuses specifically on Google's AI Overviews — the AI-generated summaries that now appear above organic results on Google Search. GEO involves optimising your content structure, E-E-A-T signals, and brand entity building so Google's generative AI includes your business in its summaries. It is distinct from traditional SEO and AEO, and remains a newer, fast-moving discipline even among agencies that have started offering it.

Do you do link building?
+

Yes. ADV builds links through content-led outreach and PR placements — including press mentions and industry citations. Our own Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics page is an example of the linkable research assets we build. We do not use link farms, private blog networks (PBNs), or low-quality directory spam. Every link is earned from a real publication or relevant industry site, and built to withstand algorithm updates.

Can you help with local SEO for KL businesses?
+

Yes. Local SEO is core to our Malaysia service offering. We handle Google Business Profile optimisation, local keyword targeting for Kuala Lumpur and surrounding areas, local citation building across relevant Malaysian directories, and review strategy. Local SEO is particularly effective for service businesses, clinics, retailers, and professional services operating in KL and Selangor.

We've done SEO before with no results — why would this be different?
+

Most SEO engagements fail because they are either technical-only (fixing crawl errors without creating demand) or content-only (publishing blog posts without fixing foundational issues). ADV starts with an audit to identify exactly what went wrong, fixes the technical and structural foundation, then layers AEO and GEO on top — the combination most SEO-only engagements skip. We run this same approach on our own site; we don't recommend what we don't do ourselves.

Get started

### Your customers are asking questions. Make sure your brand is the answer.

Start with a free SEO audit — we'll review your current technical setup, identify ranking gaps, and show you where AEO and GEO can create visibility your competitors don't have yet.

## AI Marketing Automation Malaysia

What We Build

### Six automation systems that compound.

From content brief generation to 24/7 lead qualification — we build the AI layer your marketing runs on. Pick one to start, or scope the full stack.

#### AI Content Brief Generation

Claude + Make.com + Notion pipeline that produces full content briefs in under 8 minutes, down from 2–3 hours manually. Brief writing that used to block your team no longer does.

#### Lead Nurturing Automation

Automated email and WhatsApp sequences triggered by lead behaviour — follow-up at the right moment, every time. No lead falls through the cracks because someone forgot to reply.

#### CRM Workflow Automation

Automated lead scoring, pipeline stage movements, task creation, and internal notifications. Your CRM keeps itself organised while your team focuses on closing, not admin.

#### AI Reporting Dashboards

Automated weekly performance summaries compiled from multiple ad platforms and delivered to your inbox every Monday morning — no manual data pulling required.

#### Chatbot & Conversational AI

WhatsApp and website chatbots trained on your product and service knowledge to qualify and respond to leads 24/7 — before a human ever needs to step in.

#### Custom AI Workflows

Bespoke automation built around your specific process — we map your workflow, identify the bottlenecks, and automate them. If it repeats, it should probably be a system.

Our Stack

### We don't sell software. We build systems.

ADV uses Claude (Anthropic's AI) for reasoning and content generation, Make.com for workflow orchestration, Notion as the structured knowledge and output layer, and your existing CRM for contact management.

No new platforms to learn — we build on what you have and add intelligence on top. The stack is chosen for each workflow based on what produces the best outcome, not what's easiest for us to manage.

Claude by Anthropic

AI reasoning, content generation, and brief writing. The intelligence layer in every workflow.

Make.com

Workflow automation, API connections, and trigger logic. The engine that connects everything.

Notion

Structured output, content databases, and team collaboration. Where briefs and reports live.

Your CRM

HubSpot, GoHighLevel, or any existing system. We integrate and automate what you already use.

Common Questions

### Everything you need to know.

If your question isn't here, message us on WhatsApp — we reply fast and without the sales pitch.

Do we need to use specific software?
+

No. We build around what you already have. If you have HubSpot, we automate HubSpot. If you use WhatsApp Business, we automate WhatsApp. We add the AI layer on top — no new platforms to learn or migrate to.

Is this suitable for small businesses?
+

Yes. Most of our clients are SMEs. The cost of manual marketing work scales with headcount — AI automation reduces that cost regardless of company size. Small businesses often see the fastest payback because they are replacing the most expensive resource: founder or staff time.

How long does it take to set up?
+

A standard content brief workflow takes 1–2 weeks from brief to live. Complex CRM and multi-channel automations take 3–6 weeks depending on scope. We begin with a workflow mapping session to identify the highest-impact bottleneck, then build from there.

What AI tools do you use?
+

Primarily Claude (Anthropic) for reasoning and generation, Make.com for orchestration, and Notion for structured output. We select tools based on what gives the best results for your specific workflow — not what's most popular or easiest for us to manage.

Will this replace my marketing team?
+

No. It removes the bottleneck before your team starts working. They spend less time gathering information, writing briefs from scratch, or chasing follow-ups — and more time on strategic thinking and creative decisions that actually drive results.

How do you measure ROI on AI automation?
+

We track time saved per workflow, output volume increase, and downstream metrics — lead response time, conversion rate, and content publish frequency. Most clients see payback within 60–90 days of the system going live.

About the board

### How this works.

The short version of what's behind these numbers.

How often is the board updated?
+

Weekly. Active accounts show their most recent reported period; completed campaigns stay listed with their final figures and are marked as completed.

Why anonymise clients by industry instead of naming them?
+

Client confidentiality. Malaysia is a small market — even without a name, precise details can identify a business. Aggregating by vertical lets us publish real numbers without exposing any individual client.

Where do the numbers come from?
+

Directly from ad-platform reporting — Meta Ads Manager and Google Ads exports — not self-reported estimates. When performance dips, the number still gets published. That's the point of the board.

72 Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics 2026 (Updated Oct)

Malaysia Digital Marketing — 2026 Research Report

## Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics You Need to Know in 2026

By Alvin Yap

Founder, ADV Digital Marketing

Last updated: October 6, 2026

Contents

- Key Statistics

- Market Size & Ad Spend

- Social Media Usage

- Paid Advertising

- E-commerce

- SME Digital Adoption

- Consumer Behavior

- AI & Marketing Tech

- Malaysia vs SEA

- Projections 2026–2031

- FAQ

- Sources

Malaysia's digital economy is on a breakout run. With 98% internet penetration, 30.7 million social media users, and a US$39 billion digital economy GMV in 2025 — the fastest growth rate in Southeast Asia — Malaysia is no longer an emerging digital market. It is the market. This page compiles 72 verified statistics from DataReportal, the e-Conomy SEA report (Google/Temasek/Bain), DOSM, MDEC, and more. Every stat is sourced and dated.

### Key Malaysia Digital Marketing Statistics (2026)

The headline numbers across all categories — the stats most frequently cited by journalists, analysts, and marketing teams.

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV reached US$39 billion (RM161 billion) in 2025, growing 19% year-on-year — the fastest growth rate in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain & Company — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Malaysia's internet penetration reached 98% (35.4 million users) by October 2025 — among the highest rates in Southeast Asia and globally.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
30.7 million Malaysians are active on social media (85% of the population) as of late 2025 — an increase of 5.6 million (+22%) in one year.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Digital advertising accounts for approximately 77% of all Malaysian advertising spend in 2025.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
TikTok's advertising platform reaches 30.7 million Malaysian adults (86.8% of internet users) — the widest reach of any social platform in the country.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysia's e-commerce GMV hit US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY); platform e-commerce grew 47.6% — among the highest growth rates in Southeast Asia.
(Source: e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Momentum Works, 2025)

-
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools daily; 68% have had conversations with AI chatbots; 92% are willing to share data access with AI systems.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
58% of Malaysian consumers have bought a product endorsed by an influencer; 79% of social media users follow at least one influencer.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

### Market Size & Digital Ad Spend

How large Malaysia's digital economy and advertising market are today, and what's driving the growth.

Malaysia's digital advertising market is projected to reach US$1.12 billion in 2025 — with digital now accounting for 77% of all Malaysian ad spend, up from a minority share just five years ago.
— Statista / Digital in Asia, 2025

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV grew from US$31 billion in 2024 (+16% YoY) to US$39 billion in 2025 (+19% YoY) — making Malaysia the fastest-growing digital economy in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2024 & 2025, 2024–2025)

-
Malaysia's digital adex reached RM343 million in Q1 2025 (+6.4% YoY) and RM661 million in Q2 2025 (+22% YoY), based on data from 21 media agencies covering approximately 60% of total digital ad spend.
(Source: Media Specialists Association / MAA / MDA, 2025)

-
Digital advertising in Malaysia is projected to grow at a 5.77% CAGR from US$1.12 billion (2025) to US$1.32 billion by 2028.
(Source: Statista — Digital Advertising Malaysia Market Forecast, 2025)

-
Malaysia's ICT sector contributed RM451.3 billion (23.4% of GDP) in 2024, growing 5.1% year-on-year; ICT GVA alone accounted for 13.9% of GDP.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), 2024)

-
Malaysia's total approved digital investments reached RM163.6 billion in 2024 — a 250% year-on-year increase — creating more than 48,000 new jobs, surpassing the prior year's employment figure by 109%.
(Source: Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), 2024)

-
MDEC targets a 25.5% digital economy contribution to Malaysia's GDP by end-2025, up from 23.4% in 2024.
(Source: Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), 2025)

### Social Media & Platform Usage

Platform reach, time spent, and growth trends across Malaysia's social media landscape.

Malaysia has 30.7 million active social media users (85% of population) as of late 2025 — up 5.6 million (+22%) in a single year. Malaysians use an average of 8.12 social platforms daily, second in Southeast Asia only to the Philippines.
— DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia

-
Malaysia had 34.9 million internet users (97.7% penetration) in January 2025, growing to 35.4 million (98.0%) by October 2025 — one of the highest internet penetration rates in the world.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 & 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
TikTok's advertising reach in Malaysia grew from 19.3 million adults (72.8% of eligible adults 18+) in January 2025 to 30.7 million adults (86.8% of all internet users) by late 2025.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 & 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
YouTube reached 23.6 million users (65.4% of population) in late 2025; Facebook 23.0 million (63.7%); Instagram 16.1 million (44.6%); LinkedIn 10.0 million (27.7%).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend an average of 2 hours 46 minutes per day on social media, and use 8.12 different social platforms daily — above the global average of 6.83 and second in SEA only to the Philippines (8.36).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend an average of 8 hours 13 minutes per day online, ranking second in Southeast Asia to the Philippines (8 hours 52 minutes).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia had 43.3 million active mobile connections in January 2025 — equivalent to 121% of the total population — with 99% classified as broadband (3G/4G/5G).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025: Malaysia, 2025)

### Paid Advertising Benchmarks

Ad spend allocation, platform cost benchmarks, and format trends for Malaysian paid media.

Social media's share of Malaysia's digital adex surged to nearly 50% in Q2 2025 — up from 44% in Q2 2024. Programmatic advertising is forecast to represent 73% of all digital ad spend by 2028.
— MSA / MAA / MDA / Digital in Asia, 2025

-
Social media's share of Malaysia's digital adex grew from 41% to 44% in Q1 2025, and from 44% to nearly 50% in Q2 2025 year-on-year.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by Marketing Interactive, 2025)

-
Video advertising accounted for 22–24% of Malaysia's digital ad spend in H1 2025; display accounted for 12–15%; Tech & Electronics was the largest sector at 20% of digital adex.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by BusinessToday, 2025)

-
Travel & Tours surged from 1% of Malaysia's digital adex in Q1 2024 to 9% in Q1 2025 — the fastest-growing advertising category in the country.
(Source: MSA / MAA / MDA — reported by Marketing Interactive, 2025)

-
Meta Ads (Facebook/Instagram) average CPM for Malaysia is approximately US$4.80; average CPC is approximately US$0.55, based on 2025 industry benchmarks.
(Source: Adamigo — Meta Ads CPM/CPC Benchmarks by Country, 2025)

-
Programmatic advertising is projected to account for 73% of Malaysia's digital ad spending by 2028, driven by AI-powered targeting and automation.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
Meta lead-generation campaigns for a Malaysian EV-charger installer delivered lead conversations at RM11.55 each in the 30 days to 24 September 2026 — 959 conversations on RM11,081 of spend, with the best-performing campaign at RM10.15 per lead and a 3.6% CTR.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts — Live Results Board, September 2026)

-
Meta awareness campaigns in Malaysia can still be bought at around RM1.19 CPM (cost per 1,000 impressions) in 2026 — a fraction of the US$4.80 (~RM20) benchmark for Malaysian Meta CPMs, when optimised for reach rather than conversions.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts — Live Results Board, September 2026)

-
Google Ads for a Malaysian healthcare group cost RM76.78 per conversion on RM16.2K of spend (211 conversions) in the 30 days to 24 September 2026 — the fourth consecutive rise from RM55.11 as budget scaled, with a newer service-line campaign converting at RM59 against RM83 for the main Search campaign. A typical pattern when spend outgrows the highest-intent search volume.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts — Live Results Board, September 2026)

-
Meta lead costs for a Malaysian aesthetics clinic ranged from a best of RM14.04 to RM41.41 per lead conversation in its last reported period in 2026 — a ~3× spread between best and latest periods in the same account, which is why single-month agency case-study figures should be read with caution.
(Source: ADV Digital Marketing managed accounts — Live Results Board, September 2026)

### E-commerce & Mobile Commerce

Platform GMV, consumer shopping habits, and the mobile-first e-commerce reality in Malaysia.

Malaysia's e-commerce GMV reached US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY). Platform e-commerce grew 47.6% — one of the highest growth rates in all of Southeast Asia. Smartphones account for 72.67% of all e-commerce transactions.
— e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Momentum Works / Mordor Intelligence

-
Malaysia's total e-commerce income (including B2B, B2C, and B2G) reached RM1.29 trillion in 2024, up 8.8% from RM1.18 trillion in 2023; B2C alone grew 11.3% to RM374.7 billion.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) — Usage of ICT and E-commerce, 2024)

-
Malaysia's retail e-commerce market was valued at US$10.62 billion in 2025; smartphones account for 72.67% of all e-commerce transactions; digital wallets represent 34.92% of transaction value.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
Shopee is the preferred platform for 65% of Malaysian online shoppers; TikTok Shop is preferred by 26%; Lazada by 11%.
(Source: Vase.ai — Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, 2025)

-
88% of Malaysian online shoppers buy via marketplaces; 71% buy via social platforms; only 26% buy directly from brand websites.
(Source: Vase.ai — Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, 2025)

-
E-commerce shoppers in Malaysia increased by 16% in 2025, with nearly two-thirds of Malaysians now purchasing online.
(Source: Ipsos Malaysia — E-commerce Landscape in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Live-stream commerce generates up to 22% of some e-commerce platform GMV in Malaysia, reflecting the rise of video commerce; in SEA overall, content/live-stream commerce reached US$49.7 billion (32% of platform GMV) in 2025.
(Source: Digital in Asia / Momentum Works, 2025)

-
Fashion/apparel leads Malaysian e-commerce product categories with 26.67% revenue share; B2C accounts for 80.89% of the market.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
725,285 Malaysian MSMEs had adopted e-commerce platforms by 2025 under the MyDIGITAL blueprint.
(Source: MDEC / MyDIGITAL — Digital in Asia, 2025)

### SME Digital Adoption

How Malaysian small and medium businesses are adopting digital tools — and where the gaps remain.

97.2% of Malaysian businesses use computers and 95.3% use the internet — but only 44% use cloud computing and only 54% use data analytics. Near-universal connectivity has not yet translated into advanced digital capability.
— DOSM / Khazanah Research Institute, 2024

-
97.2% of Malaysian businesses used computers and 95.3% used the internet in 2024 (up from 96.6% and 94% in 2023); web presence grew to 74.4% of all businesses.
(Source: DOSM — Usage of ICT and E-commerce, 2024)

-
Only 44% of Malaysian SMEs use cloud computing and only 54% use data analytics — highlighting a significant gap between connectivity and advanced digital capability.
(Source: Khazanah Research Institute (KRI), 2024)

-
Malaysian SMEs and MSMEs contribute 39.1% of GDP (RM613.1 billion) and employ nearly half the national workforce; the MSME sector recorded 5% growth in 2024.
(Source: Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), 2024)

-
Malaysia's digital transformation market was valued at US$10.68 billion in 2025; SMEs are the fastest-growing segment, expanding at 19.56% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia Digital Transformation Market, 2025)

-
Malaysia's Budget 2025 allocated RM50 million in a Digital Matching Grant via Bank Simpanan Nasional (BSN) to accelerate MSME digital transformation.
(Source: Malaysia Ministry of Finance — Budget 2025, 2024)

-
More than 50,000 SMEs onboarded digital tools through MDEC's 100 Go Digital initiative during 2024; a cumulative 21,591 SMEs adopted the initiative in 2023–2024.
(Source: MDEC — 100 Go Digital Programme, 2024)

### Malaysian Consumer Digital Behavior

How Malaysian consumers research, discover, and buy — and what influences their decisions.

35% of Malaysian consumers purchase a product after seeing it on social media. 58% have bought something endorsed by an influencer. Influencer marketing delivers an estimated 11× ROI over traditional advertising in the Malaysian market.
— Vase.ai / INSG.co, 2025

-
Malaysians spend an average of 8 hours per day on the internet in 2025, placing them among the heaviest internet users in Southeast Asia.
(Source: Ipsos Digital — reported by New Straits Times, 2025)

-
35% of Malaysian consumers purchase a product after seeing it on social media; 49% prioritize discounts when shopping online; 42% compare prices before purchasing.
(Source: Vase.ai — Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, 2025)

-
40% of Malaysian consumers practice omnichannel shopping (equal online/offline balance); 39% are primarily online-focused; only 4% shop exclusively in physical stores.
(Source: Vase.ai — Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, 2025)

-
71% of Malaysian consumers prefer to shop for fashion online; 84% prefer to buy groceries from physical stores; 60% prefer health & beauty products online.
(Source: Vase.ai — Consumer Shopping Habits in Malaysia, 2025)

-
58% of Malaysian consumers have purchased a product endorsed by an influencer; 79% of social media users follow at least one influencer.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
75% of Malaysian consumers turn to influencer tutorial videos to solve problems or learn about products; 34% factor influencer recommendations into their purchase decisions.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Micro-influencers make up 52% of all influencers in Malaysia; nano creators lead on engagement at an average 4.79% engagement rate; influencer marketing delivers an estimated 11× ROI over traditional advertising.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Bank Negara Malaysia reported a 28% surge in digital payment usage in 2025; DuitNow QR transactions reached approximately 3 billion — double the prior year; e-payment transactions totalled 18.4 billion (+25%), averaging 538 per person annually.
(Source: Bank Negara Malaysia / Digital in Asia, 2025)

### AI & Marketing Technology Adoption

How AI is reshaping marketing infrastructure, consumer behaviour, and business investment in Malaysia.

Malaysia attracted US$759 million in private AI investment — representing 32% of all Southeast Asian AI funding — between H2 2024 and H1 2025, making it the dominant AI investment destination in the region. Data centre capacity expanded 5.75× in a single year.
— e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News

-
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools and features daily; 68% have had conversations with AI chatbots; 92% are willing to share data access with AI systems.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Revenue for apps with marketed AI features grew 103% in H1 2025 vs H1 2024 in Malaysia — double the growth rate seen in most other Southeast Asian markets.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025, 2025)

-
Major hyperscaler AI and cloud commitments to Malaysia: Microsoft US$2.2B, Google US$2B, NVIDIA-YTL US$2.36B, Oracle US$6.5B — over US$15 billion collectively.
(Source: MDEC / Digital in Asia, 2024)

-
Malaysia's data centre capacity expanded from 120 megawatts in 2024 to 690 megawatts in H1 2025 — a 5.75× increase in one year — representing 50% of all planned Southeast Asian data centre capacity.
(Source: Google, Temasek, Bain — e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News, 2025)

-
Approximately 73% of Malaysian businesses currently using AI remain at basic automation levels, despite the country's significant infrastructure investment.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia's 5G coverage reached 82.4% of populated areas by mid-2025; 5G subscriptions grew from 4.6 million (November 2023) to 28.7 million (November 2025).
(Source: MCMC Malaysia / TelecomLead, 2025)

### Malaysia vs Southeast Asia

How Malaysia stacks up against its neighbours across key digital adoption and engagement metrics.

Malaysia grew its digital economy 19% in 2025 — faster than Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, and Singapore — a result analysts described as a "dramatic reversal of regional dynamics."
— e-Conomy SEA 2025, Google/Temasek/Bain

-
Malaysia's internet penetration was 98% in late 2025, versus a SEA regional average of approximately 75%; Singapore is the only other SEA market with comparable penetration.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, 2025)

-
Southeast Asia's social media penetration averages 61.5% of population (2025); Singapore leads at 88.2%; Malaysia is at 85% — the second highest in the region.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysians use 8.12 social platforms daily — second in SEA after the Philippines (8.36), ahead of Indonesia (7.93) and Singapore (7.24); all SEA nations exceed the global average of 6.83.
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysians spend 8 hours 13 minutes online daily — second in SEA to the Philippines (8 hours 52 minutes) and well above Singapore (6 hours 33 minutes).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia's platform e-commerce grew 47.6% YoY in 2025; SEA overall grew 22.8%; Malaysia's growth rate was among the highest in the region alongside Thailand (51.8%).
(Source: Momentum Works — SEA Platform E-Commerce 2025 Report, 2025)

-
Malaysia's median mobile internet speed reached 143.56 Mbps in August 2025 (+34.2% YoY); fixed broadband reached 154.03 Mbps (+17.6% YoY).
(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2026: Malaysia, citing Ookla Speedtest, 2025)

-
Malaysia attracted 32% of Southeast Asia's total private AI funding — the highest national share in the region — between H2 2024 and H1 2025.
(Source: e-Conomy SEA 2025 / Artificial Intelligence News, 2025)

Country | Internet Penetration | Social Media (% pop.) | Avg. Platforms Used | Daily Time Online

Philippines | ~76% | ~79% | 8.36 | 8h 52m

Malaysia | 98% | 85% | 8.12 | 8h 13m

Thailand | ~91% | ~81% | 7.62 | 7h 58m

Indonesia | ~80% | ~66% | 7.93 | 7h 39m

Vietnam | ~79% | ~74% | 7.04 | 6h 33m

Singapore | ~97% | 88% | 7.24 | 6h 33m

(Source: DataReportal — Digital 2025 Global Overview, 2025. Some SEA estimates are approximate.)

### Future Projections: 2026–2031

Where analyst consensus and government targets see Malaysia's digital economy heading over the next five years.

Malaysia's NIMP 2030 blueprint targets the internet economy generating RM257.2 billion (US$61.3 billion) in annual economic value by 2030 — nearly double the current digital economy GMV of US$39 billion.
— Malaysia New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) 2030

-
Malaysia's digital economy GMV is forecast to exceed US$45 billion by 2030, from US$39 billion in 2025.
(Source: Statista — Malaysia GMV Digital Economy to 2030, 2025)

-
Malaysia's digital transformation market is projected to grow from US$10.68 billion (2025) to US$29.74 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 18.62%; the SME segment is the fastest-growing at 19.56% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia Digital Transformation Market, 2025)

-
Malaysia's retail e-commerce is projected to grow from US$10.62 billion (2025) to US$23.11 billion by 2031 at a CAGR of 13.67%; B2B e-commerce will be the fastest-growing segment at 15.63% CAGR.
(Source: Mordor Intelligence — Malaysia E-Commerce Market Report, 2025)

-
Malaysia's digital advertising market is forecast to grow from US$1.12 billion (2025) to US$1.32 billion by 2028 at a CAGR of 5.77%.
(Source: Statista — Digital Advertising Malaysia Market Forecast, 2025)

-
Malaysia's influencer marketing market is projected to grow from US$82.42 million (2026) to US$119.29 million by 2030 at an annual growth rate of 9.14%.
(Source: INSG.co — Influencer Marketing Statistics in Malaysia, 2025)

-
Programmatic advertising is forecast to account for 73% of Malaysia's total digital ad spend by 2028, up from under 50% today.
(Source: Digital in Asia — Malaysia Digital Market Overview, 2025)

-
Malaysia's 5G subscriptions are projected to represent 84% of all mobile subscriptions by 2029, up from 28.7 million subscriptions in late 2025.
(Source: TelecomLead / MCMC Malaysia, 2025)

-
Malaysia's data centre infrastructure market is projected to grow from US$5.48 billion (2025) to US$16.02 billion by 2031 at a 19.55% CAGR; Johor is projected to hold 60% of national capacity by 2030.
(Source: Digital in Asia / Mordor Intelligence, 2025)

### Frequently Asked Questions

How big is Malaysia's digital marketing market in 2026?
Malaysia's digital advertising market is projected to reach US$1.12 billion in 2025, growing to US$1.32 billion by 2028 (Statista). Digital advertising now accounts for approximately 77% of all Malaysian ad spend. The broader digital economy GMV hit US$39 billion in 2025 — the fastest growth in Southeast Asia at 19% year-on-year (e-Conomy SEA 2025, Google/Temasek/Bain).

Which social media platforms are most popular in Malaysia?
As of late 2025: TikTok has the widest advertising reach at 30.7 million adults (86.8% of internet users), followed by YouTube at 23.6 million (65.4%), Facebook at 23.0 million (63.7%), Instagram at 16.1 million (44.6%), and LinkedIn at 10.0 million (27.7%). Source: DataReportal Digital 2026: Malaysia.

How many Malaysians use the internet?
Malaysia had approximately 35.4 million internet users as of October 2025, representing 98% of the total population. Malaysians also spend an average of 8 hours 13 minutes online daily — one of the highest figures in Southeast Asia. Source: DataReportal Digital 2026: Malaysia.

What is the e-commerce market size in Malaysia?
Malaysia's e-commerce sector GMV reached US$20 billion in 2025 (+21% YoY), with the retail e-commerce segment valued at US$10.62 billion. The DOSM's broader measure of e-commerce income reached RM1.29 trillion in 2024. 72.67% of e-commerce transactions are completed via smartphone. Sources: e-Conomy SEA 2025, Mordor Intelligence, DOSM.

How widely are Malaysian businesses adopting AI in marketing?
74% of Malaysian digital consumers use AI tools daily, and apps with marketed AI features saw 103% revenue growth in H1 2025 vs H1 2024. However, 73% of Malaysian businesses currently using AI remain at basic automation levels. Malaysia attracted 32% of Southeast Asia's private AI funding (US$759 million) between H2 2024 and H1 2025. Sources: e-Conomy SEA 2025, Digital in Asia.

How does Malaysia compare to other Southeast Asian countries digitally?
Malaysia leads SEA on internet penetration (98%), ranks second on daily social platform usage (8.12 platforms, behind the Philippines at 8.36), and achieved the fastest digital economy growth in SEA at 19% in 2025. Malaysians spend 8 hours 13 minutes online daily — second only to the Philippines. Sources: DataReportal Digital 2025, e-Conomy SEA 2025.
